featured_reviews.name: Chef Vaidehi Pathare
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was my second visit to Pangat in Nancy Colony, Borivali. I had a good experience earlier, so I came again on a rainy Friday evening with my family. It took us a good 15 minutes to get a table. The restaurant has both indoor and outdoor seating. This time we chose to sit inside. The place looks classy with minimalistic decor, and I liked the overall ambience.

We started with Veg Manchow Soup, Chicken Kalimiri Kebab, and Crab Lollipop. The soup was perfect for the weather and tasted really good. The Chicken Kalimiri Kebab tasted good and was cooked well, but I found a thread in the last piece, which was really disappointing. The staff took it to the kitchen when we showed it, but there was no response after that from their end. The Crab Lollipop tasted like it was frozen and not freshly made in their kitchen. Definitely not something I would order again.

For the main course, we ordered Veg Thali, Chicken Hyderabadi, Jeera Rice, Chapati, and Rice Bhakri. The thali was nice and filling. The Chicken Hyderabadi had good flavours but I personally felt it could have been a bit spicier. It had more of spinach-like aftertaste. The Rice Bhakri was soft and fresh, which I really liked. The Chapati was good and the Jeera Rice was simple and comforting.

The food overall was decent, but the service needs a lot of improvement. We had to call the staff multiple times just to get water or basic things. Many times, they completely ignored us, which was disappointing. When I raised this with the manager, he just listened and didn’t say anything. I honestly feel service matters as much as the food, and that part really fell short during our visit. I have had a better experience here before, so I do hope they take this feedback positively.

Ratings:
Quality - 3/5
Quantity - 4/5
Service - 3/5
Price - ₹2100 for 4 people

For more mouthwatering food content, don’t forget to follow @chefvaidehipathare on Instagram!

owner_posts.post_text:
The secret to incredible coastal food lies entirely in the authenticity of its spices. At Aamcho Kokan – The Family Restaurant, we do not believe in shortcuts or pre-packaged spice mixes. We source our red chilies, peppercorns, and coriander seeds directly from regional farmers, ensuring that our kitchen delivers the genuine, fiery kick that has made us the best Kokan restaurant in Borivali. When you dine with us, you are experiencing the true soul of coastal Maharashtra. 🌴😋

Our menu is a masterclass in authentic Malwani food and traditional Marathi cuisine. Our chefs use traditional stone-grinding techniques to prepare our masalas, which preserves the essential oils of the spices and creates a deep, multi-layered flavor profile. Whether you are biting into our slow-cooked mutton rassa or savoring a vegetarian patwadi rassa, you will instantly notice the brightness and complexity that only fresh, handcrafted ingredients can provide. 🍛🌶️

For the ultimate culinary tour of our menu, nothing beats our signature Fish Thalis. We believe a thali should be a complete sensory experience. That is why our platters are meticulously balanced, pairing the bold, sharp heat of our fish curries with the cooling, soothing creaminess of fresh Solkadhi. Toss in some hot, pillowy bhakris or crispy rice vadas, and you have a meal that satisfies your deep-seated cravings while honoring centuries of coastal culinary tradition. 🐟🌾

While we are fiercely proud of our coastal roots, we believe that a truly great family restaurant should offer a world of culinary options. At Aamcho Kokan – The Family Restaurant, we combine our deep expertise in seafood with a spectacular multi-cuisine menu. This unique balance has earned us a reputation as the best seafood restaurant in Borivali East, where every single diner finds exactly what they are craving. 🐟🦀🦐

For the seafood lovers in your group, we offer an unparalleled experience. Our fresh Prawns, crabs, and premium fish are cooked using authentic coastal recipes that deliver bold, unforgettable flavors. If you want to experience the absolute best of what our kitchen has to offer, our famous Fish Thalis provide a magnificent spread of textures and spices that represent the very pinnacle of traditional coastal dining. It is a complete, wholesome feast on a single plate. 🍛🍤

But our culinary journey doesn't stop at the shoreline. To cater to diverse tastes, our talented chefs also cook up phenomenal Asian, Chinese, Indian, and Tandoori cuisines. Whether someone in your family wants a rich, buttery North Indian curry with garlic naan, or a fiery plate of Chinese Schezwan noodles, our kitchen prepares each dish with absolute authenticity and premium ingredients. It’s the ultimate destination for group dining. 🍜🥢🔥

Our dining room is thoughtfully designed with plush, comfortable seating, ensuring that large families can gather and dine with ease.

For many Mumbai foodies, a perfectly fried, crispy Bombil is the ultimate comfort food. The contrast between the crunchy exterior and the delicate, melt-in-your-mouth fish inside is pure perfection. At Aamcho Kokan – The Family Restaurant, we take this classic dish to new heights, cementing our position as the premier best seafood restaurant in Borivali East. If you appreciate masterfully fried seafood, you need to visit us immediately. 🐟🍟

Our legendary Bombay Duck fry is prepared using time-tested methods, lightly coating the fresh fish in a seasoned rava batter before frying it to a perfect, non-greasy golden crisp. It’s the ultimate starter to kick off an extraordinary meal of authentic Malwani food. Our chefs understand the delicate nature of coastal fish, ensuring that every piece remains incredibly moist, juicy, and packed with natural flavor. 🍤🔥

To turn your meal into an absolute feast, pair your starters with one of our comprehensive Fish Thalis. Featuring an array of robust curries, traditional flatbreads, rice, and cooling Solkadhi, our thalis offer a complete tour of the Konkan coast's rich culinary map. It is a deeply hearty meal that satisfies cravings completely, making us the top dining choice for local seafood enthusiasts. 🍛🌶️

In the coastal villages of the Konkan region, hospitality is a way of life. Guests are treated like family, and meals are prepared with an abundance of love, freshness, and spice. Aamcho Kokan – The Family Restaurant was founded to bring that exact philosophy to Mumbai. We are immensely proud to be known as the best Kokan restaurant in Borivali, offering an authentic taste of coastal warmth and incredible regional food. 🌴😋

Our restaurant’s design mirrors the welcoming nature of a coastal home. Featuring spacious, comfortable seating, our venue is built for long, joyful meals where food is shared and celebrated. Whether you are introducing your children to the flavors of your childhood or enjoying a relaxed weekend lunch with friends, our comforting ambiance provides the perfect setting for making beautiful memories over incredible plates of food. 🍽️❤️

Our menu is anchored by our magnificent Fish Thalis. Each thali is a curated feast, showcasing the very best of our kitchen’s capabilities. From the fiery, perfectly balanced fish curries to the immaculate, crispy fried fish starters, every element on the platter is designed to harmonize beautifully. It is a deeply satisfying dining experience that captures the true essence of traditional coastal cooking in every single bite. 🍛🌶

Our kitchen treats shellfish with the utmost care. Our Crab preparations are legendary, simmered in thick, intensely aromatic masalas that allow the natural sweetness of the crab meat to shine through. Similarly, our Prawns are sourced daily to ensure maximum crispness and flavor, whether they are tossed on a hot tawa with local spices or fried to a beautiful golden crunch. We invite you to join us in our beautiful dining room, which features comfortable seating that is perfect for everything from intimate date nights to massive family reunions.

From the rich, comforting depth of our chicken rassa to the beautifully textured vegetarian specialties, every item on our menu is designed to evoke a sense of warmth and nostalgia. We preserve the old ways of cooking because we believe true flavor cannot be rushed. 🌴😋

We have created a bright, cheerful dining room with spacious, comfortable seating that invites you to linger over your meal, chat with loved ones, and create lasting memories. We believe that dining out should be a relaxing escape from the hustle and bustle of city life, and our warm hospitality reflects that philosophy completely. 🍛🌶️

To experience our culinary variety all on one plate, look no further than our incredible Fish Thalis. Every dish is a testament to the timeless cooking techniques of the Maharashtra coast. 🍤🔥

The Konkan coastline of India is famous for its breathtaking beaches, swaying palm trees, and above all, its fiercely flavorful food. Aamcho Kokan – The Family Restaurant was born out of a passion to bring these incredible, unadulterated culinary traditions straight to the heart of Mumbai’s suburbs. Today, we are immensely proud to be recognized as the best Kokan restaurant in Borivali, offering an escape into a world of rich spices and deep coastal heritage. 🌴😋

Our kitchen specializes in authentic Malwani food and traditional Marathi cuisine. We avoid modern shortcuts, choosing instead to slow-cook our gravies, hand-grind our masalas, and roast our grated coconuts over an open flame to release their natural oils. This meticulous process gives our dishes an incredible depth of flavor. A standout highlight of our menu is our signature Crab masala—cooked in a thick, fiery red gravy that perfectly complements the sweet, tender meat of the crab. It’s a messy, hands-on, and utterly blissful dining experience. 🦀🌶️

What makes a truly exceptional thali? It’s not just the variety of items on the plate; it’s the harmony of flavors, the freshness of the catch, and the soul behind the cooking. At Aamcho Kokan – The Family Restaurant, we have elevated the humble thali into an art form. As the undisputed best seafood restaurant in Borivali East, we invite you to experience a culinary masterpiece that defines the very essence of coastal dining. 🍛🐠

When you order one of our famous Fish Thalis, you are treated to a glorious spread that honors authentic Malwani food traditions. The star of the plate is, of course, your choice of fish—be it the delicate, crispy Bombay Duck, a grand, meaty slice of Pomfret, or sweet, succulent prawns. This is accompanied by a deeply spiced, coconut-based gravy that begs to be soaked up with warm, handmade bhakris or traditional rice vadas. A small bowl of tangy, pink Solkadhi acts as the perfect digestif, rounding out an incredible meal. 🌶️🌾

The secret to our success lies in our unwavering commitment to freshness. We work closely with local suppliers to secure the best catch of the day, ensuring that every fish served is sweet, firm, and entirely free of compromise. This dedication to quality is why seafood enthusiasts from all over the city gather at our restaurant, making us a bustling hub of happy diners every afternoon and evening. 🦀🦐

featured_reviews.review_text: Authentic taste of konkani food. We just happened to be there for Sunday lunch. The ambience is good. Prompt service. Delicious food. featured_reviews.name: Priyam Saha
featured_reviews.review_text: An outstanding dining experience awaits you at *Aamcho Kokan*. Don't let the name confuse you; it also offers some remarkable Pan-Asian cuisine. The flavors, service, and cleanliness are all exceptional. The prices are quite reasonable considering the high quality of food and service provided. It's truly worth every cent. Each dish boasts perfectly balanced flavors, with ingredients that are incredibly fresh and cooked to perfection! A special shoutout to Jayesh, who took excellent care of us and recommended fantastic dishes such as Crispy Lotus Stem Shaoxing Sriracha, Chicken Korean Spicy, Korean Spicy Ramen, Wok Tossed Cottage Cheese Teriyaki, Khepsa Biryani, and many more. Thank you for the amazing meal!!!!!

featured_reviews.review_text:

featured_reviews.name: Shweta Sawant
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Amcho Kokan is a hidden gem for anyone who loves authentic Konkani and Maharashtrian food. The taste is absolutely homely – from perfectly spiced Kombdi Vade to crispy Bombil Fry, every dish feels like it’s made with love.

The ambience is warm and rustic, with old Marathi songs playing in the background that add a beautiful nostalgic touch. Great service, generous portions, and fair pricing.

Highly recommend if you’re looking for traditional flavors and a cozy, cultural vibe. Will definitely be coming back.

During the day, it is family-friendly and relaxed, but as the evening progresses, the energy shifts with live music and upbeat lighting, making it a popular spot for birthday celebrations and group hangouts.

The menu is impressively diverse, spanning North Indian, Continental, and Chinese cuisines. A must-try for vegetarians is the Paneer Tikka Pizza. Unlike generic mall pizzas, this version features:
The Crust: A well-baked base that provides a sturdy crunch without being overly doughy.
The Toppings: Generous chunks of paneer that have been properly marinated in traditional tandoori spices, giving the pizza a distinct smoky flavor.

The service is generally hospitable, though it can get a bit slow during peak weekend hours or when live performances are in full swing.

Whether you’re stopping by after a movie at INOX or looking for a lively dinner spot, The Boat Club is a solid choice for its creative theme and reliable fusion dishes.

featured_reviews.name: Janhavi Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Goankar Cuisine in Mumbai, and overall it turned out to be a mixed but interesting dining experience. When we first arrived, the restaurant was completely empty, but as we started ordering, the place quickly became busy and was soon filled with many guests.

We began with crab Manchow soup, but honestly it tasted more like a regular Manchow soup as the crab quantity was very minimal and there wasn’t much seafood flavour in it. After that, we tried prawns lollipop, which unfortunately was not good. The texture felt sticky and unusual, and it was difficult to even recognize the prawns properly, so we didn’t enjoy that dish.

However, the experience improved with the next dishes. The squid Koliwada was excellent — very crunchy and perfectly cooked. It was definitely one of the better starters we tried.

The staff member Mr. Akash, who was serving us, was very helpful and gave good suggestions. On his recommendation, we tried chicken Kalakari, which turned out to be really tasty. It had a rich, authentic Indian-style chicken masala and was well marinated with great flavour.

For the main course, he first suggested chicken vindaloo, but since it is slightly tangy, we decided not to order it. Instead, he recommended chicken Xacuti (Shakoti), which was excellent and full of authentic Goan flavours. Along with that, we tried prawns masala dry, which was honestly amazing and one of the highlights of the meal.

We paired the dishes with Amboli, Ghavna, and rice bhakri. The rice bhakri was very large and quite filling, making it a great accompaniment to the curries.

For dessert, we tried Ukdiche Modak ice cream, which was truly a game changer. It was such a unique dessert that we ended up ordering another one because everyone at the table loved it. It was a really creative and delicious twist on the traditional modak.

Overall, despite a few disappointing starters, the main course, dessert, and the helpful service by Mr. Akash made the experience really enjoyable. If you visit, definitely try the squid Koliwada, prawns masala dry, chicken Xacuti, and the Ukdiche Modak ice cream.

featured_reviews.name: Vinayak Moorthy
featured_reviews.review_text:
Goaikar – where the fish is larger than life and the flavours come with a warning ⚠️🐟

Walked into Goaikar with big Goan expectations and walked out with an even bigger respect for their humongous fish portions. Let’s start with the clear winners of the day — the prawns lollipop and the stuffed bombil fry. Absolute show-stealers. Crisp, juicy, perfectly seasoned… the kind of dishes that make you nod silently while chewing because words fail you.

Next up, the iconic Goan ros omelette with poee — decent, comforting, but didn’t quite give us that nostalgic roadside Goan punch. More “okay okay” than “arre waah”.

Now to the grand thali saga 🍽️
We ordered the Surmai fish thali, Pomfret special thali, and Bombil thali — and oh my God, the fishes were MONSTERS. Fried to golden perfection, fresh, meaty, and clearly not shy about their presence on the plate. Total paisa-vasool when it comes to the fish itself.

But (there’s always a but)… the accompanying curries and gravies came in hot — and not the fun kind 🌶️🔥
For us, especially with a Goan mom in the house, the gravies felt too spicy and a little off-track from traditional Goan flavours. More fire, less finesse. Authentic Goa whispered… while chilli shouted.

Just when our taste buds were waving a white flag, dessert arrived like a saviour from heaven — Ukdiche Modak Ice Cream 🍨✨
Sweet, comforting, innovative, and honestly the icing on the cake (or modak on the ice cream?). A perfect, soulful ending that brought smiles back instantly.

From a value standpoint, pricing sits firmly at the premium end, with most dishes priced at ₹500 and above. While the generous seafood portions partially justify this, the ukdiche modak ice cream, though innovative and flavourful, was served in a modest portion at ₹180, feeling more like a tasting than a finale.

It is also worth noting that several social media claims suggesting a 10% discount at the restaurant did not reflect our experience, and no such concession was available during our visit—something diners may wish to verify in advance.

What truly elevated the experience was the service. Our order taker, Aditya, was exceptionally warm, attentive, and knowledgeable, guiding us with genuine enthusiasm. The entire service team mirrored this standard—courteous, efficient, and consistently welcoming—adding a layer of hospitality that made the meal feel relaxed and well cared for.

Final verdict:
Goaikar nails seafood portions and frying like a boss, experiments boldly with flavours, and redeems everything with dessert magic. A must-visit for fish lovers — just keep a glass of water (and an open mind for spice) handy 😄🔥🐠

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (minus half a star for the chilli ambush)

The Malvani Chicken Thali was especially delicious with its spicy and traditional taste. The Mutton Thali was flavorful and satisfying and the Fish Thali was fresh and very tasty.

A great place for anyone who loves Malvani food. Highly recommended for a fulfilling and tasty meal.❤️😍

featured_reviews.name: Ameya Banavali
featured_reviews.review_text:
Worst experience on Diwali day!!
Pity the owners because the server threatened customers that they will hit them and the owners would not say anything

Detailed review
I visited today at 1:50 pm. There were people in waiting outside.
After waiting for 6 minutes, a server came out to inform that there was a notebook kept at the side which the customer had to note down their booking by themselves for (no staff to do this)

After waiting for half an hour in the sweltering heat, we (myself, wife and father in law ) got a seat at the further most corner. The one and only AC in the place was running at full throttle but it failed to provide cooling to the crowded room full of customers.

We had already chosen our choice of orders during our wait outside.

Order for :
- Mutton Thali
- Extra Chapati
- Extra Bhakri
- Bombil Fry
- Chicken Poppers
- Alani Bhaat
- Thumbs up half ltr.

After waiting for another 10 mins seated on the table, the server (same guy as earlier) came and took our order very efficiently. 👍

This was at around 2:30 pm. As it was too late for lunch already, we instructed the waiter to get our orders as soon as they were prepared.

The server promptly got the coldrink and plonked the bottle on the table without serving and left. Then we waited and waited and waited.... And waited some more....
In-between we asked the waiter 5 times about when we could see some food on our table his reply everytime was " bas aa rahaa hai"

So after waiting till 3 pm after my senior citizen father in law started getting agitated, (by this time the bombil had been served to us by a lady). At this point I asked the waiter in a loud voice about rest  of my order, The moment I raised my voice, the waiter started shouting back and threatened to hit me.

When the matter escalated, another guy, seemingly the owner came to our table to sort out the matter , he confessed theybwere short on staff  today (not my problem but still)

The lady also intervened and then on she cooled the situation with prompt service and the required attention.

On the food front
Bombil were oily
Mutton was chewy
Poppers were good
Alani Bhaat was excellent

Trigger points-
- This hotel doesnt even have a working washbasin for customers to rinse post meal. Please bear in mind that these people serve fish.
- The AC is pathetic which brings upon a strange discomfort while eating.
- An uncle is a safari suit who was from the restaurant team and claimed be from some food department told that everything is made fresh.  This explains the chewy undercooked mutton as you need to cook mutton for atleast an hour, and simmer before dishing it out.
-Total bill was 1780.

Post meal review-
- At the time of writing this detailed review I am feeling acidic reflux and so is my wife which indicates the quality of ingredients used.

Dear owners
- Your food is pathetic.
- Your ambience is meh.
- Not to be classist but your service is good probably for the slums, not IC Colony.

P.S. I have also messaged my friend who recommended your restaurant to stay away henceforth.

Happy Diwali!
